summary: Root cause identified: the external exchange partner (api.exchange-partner.example, reached via exchange-api/exchange-gateway) became unresponsive starting ~11:01Z, producing 5000ms upstream connect timeouts and 503s at exchange-gateway, which surface as 504s on order-service's submit path (~30% error rate, p99 ~150ms -> ~4.3s). Confidence is medium (0.78): the downstream chain, the caller-independent blast radius (order-service and market-data-service, the gateway's two independent callers, both degrade in the 11:01Z bucket while non-callers stay flat) and the absence of any gateway-internal resource saturation (CPU/memory/request_rate flat, zero restarts, only upstream_latency_ms exploding 120ms -> ~9000ms) are all observed; the final hop is inferred because exchange-api has has_telemetry:false. The order-service v2.15.2 release (dep-5333) and the pricing-engine cfg-2290 change are not the cause: the release cannot produce failures in two other never-deployed services, and its 11:16Z rollback did not restore service. Shared platform components (ledger-db/redis-cache/kafka) are contradicted or off the failing call path. Do not expect the rollback to have fixed this — the remediation is exchange route failover, not order-service rollback.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange partner / exchange-api outage causing exchange-gateway upstream timeouts
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external exchange provider (api.exchange-partner.example / exchange-api) degraded at ~11:01Z, causing 5000ms upstream connect timeouts and 503s at exchange-gateway, which surface as 504s on order-service's submit path and as stale-quote warnings / elevated error rate (but not latency) at market-data-service. Residual uncertainty: the failing hop is beyond exchange-api (has_telemetry:false), so the partner-side origin is inferred from exchange-gateway's upstream_latency_ms proxy, not directly observed.

causal_chain.claim: exchange-gateway's upstream call to the external partner stalls: 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder' from 11:01:25Z, then 'exchange-api returned 503' from 11:02:20Z; circuit breaker OPEN at 11:03:26Z.
exchange-gateway p99 latency jumps ~130ms -> 4625ms avg and error rate to ~44.7% steady, dominated by the stuck 5000ms upstream call.

The latency is on exchange-gateway's upstream_latency_ms (120ms -> ~7450-9500ms) while its own cpu (~27-32%), memory (~40-49%), request_rate (~272 req/s) and restarts (0) stay flat across onset -> the stall originates outside the gateway process, not from internal resource saturation.

exchange-gateway had zero deployments and zero config changes in the preceding week, and no deployment/config change occurred for ANY service in the 10:50-12:59 onset window -> no internal change introduced the fault and the shared platform components were untouched.

A second, structurally independent caller of exchange-gateway degrades on the same 11:01 bucket: market-data-service error_rate 0.24% -> ~6.5% with its sole log signature 'stale quotes ... via exchange-gateway'; it shares no datastore with exchange-gateway. (Severity differs: its own p99 stays ~40ms flat and it emitted zero ERROR logs, so the shared element is the exchange-gateway/exchange-feed path, not an identical failure mode.)
order-service, calling exchange-gateway for placeOrder, receives 504 Gateway Timeout -> ~30% error rate and 4286ms p99, all 349 error logs being the single downstream-blaming signature.
order-service v2.15.2 rollback at 11:16Z did not restore service; errors persisted to 12:58Z, consistent with an external cause the rollback cannot touch.

assumptions: The 5000ms connect timeout to api.exchange-partner.example reflects partner-side unresponsiveness rather than a network path fault between exchange-gateway and the partner (exchange-api has has_telemetry:false, so the true first failing hop is permanently unobservable)
The 503 'exchange-api returned 503' lines originate from the partner side rather than from an intermediary not represented in the graph
11:00-11:01Z is the true onset rather than a transient cycle (earliest evidence anywhere is 11:01:25Z; order-service's bucket boundary is 11:00)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared platform component (ledger-db / kafka) degradation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared platform data component (ledger-db or kafka) degraded, independently of any release, producing timeouts on the order-service submit path. Largely excluded by measurement: the two other ledger-db callers stay at baseline and ledger-db's only exposed health signal is flat, though kafka/redis remain unmeasured.

causal_chain.claim: order-service has db/queue edges to the shared components ledger-db and kafka (redis-cache is NOT on its path).
A ledger-db fault would be expected to co-produce symptoms in its other callers (portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service) as well as order-service.

Contradicted by measurement: portfolio-service and settlement-service remain flat at ~0.2% error and flat p99 through the 11:00-11:02Z onset, payment-service stays ~0.2%, and ledger-db's only retrievable health metric (cpu_pct ~30%) is flat.
The fault instead tracks the exchange-gateway path, which is caller-independent across order-service and market-data-service at 11:01-11:02Z.

assumptions: A shared component degraded even though no change event lands on it in the window (F19/F23) and kafka/redis-cache health metrics were never retrieved

ranked_hypotheses.title: Pre-existing / flapping condition unrelated to the release
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 30% failure rate reflects a condition independent of this morning's release; the rollback will not (and did not) fix it.

causal_chain.claim: Rollback at 11:16Z did not coincide with recovery; errors persisted to 12:58Z.
Errors originate at exchange-gateway, which had no change of its own.

assumptions: The condition began near 11:00Z rather than truly 'pre-existing'; the error-rate jump is sharp and simultaneous across two callers at 11:00-11:01Z, so it is new
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: F7 shows a sharp, sustained jump from ~0.2% to ~30% at the 11:00 bucket, and F30/F31 show the same-minute onset at a second independent caller (market-data-service) — the condition is new and has a localized origin (exchange-gateway's upstream call), not a pre-existing flap. This collapses into H2 with an external trigger.

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.15.2 regression (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The idempotency-key change in order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333) introduced a regression in the submit path, producing 504s on order submit.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5333 (order-service v2.15.2, 'Add idempotency keys to order submit') deployed 10:48Z.
order-service error rate jumps ~0.2% -> ~30% and p99 ~150ms -> ~4286ms at the 11:00 bucket, ~12 min after deploy.
order-service emits 504s on submit.

assumptions: The idempotency-key code path is on the order submit path and could produce a 504 (no finding shows the mechanism)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: All order-service errors are a single downstream-blaming signature (F8); exchange-gateway shows the origin one minute earlier (F9) with latency on its upstream call (F29); a second, independent, never-deployed caller (market-data-service) degrades in the same minute (F30/F31/F35). A fault inside order-service's code cannot produce failures in exchange-gateway and market-data-service. Rollback at 11:16Z did not restore service (F13).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Order-service rollout incomplete/mixed-version — only some instances faulting
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Only a fraction of order-service instances took v2.15.2, and those instances fail, producing a partial ~30% error rate.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5333 deployed 10:48Z and rolled back 11:16Z.
~30% (not 100%) of order submissions fail, consistent with a subset of bad instances.

assumptions: No per-pod rollout timeline exists; the mixed-version premise is entirely unverified
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: The failure signature is uniform and downstream (F8) with the origin in exchange-gateway from 11:01:25Z (F9); a mixed-version fraction of order-service pods cannot produce failures at exchange-gateway and market-data-service (F31). Errors persisted past rollback (F13). No rollout-timeline evidence exists.

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine cache TTL config change (cfg-2290) propagating quote latency
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Reducing pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 at 09:20Z increased downstream quote latency, contributing to order-submit failures.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2290 changes pricing-engine cache TTL 5->4 at 09:20Z.
Order submit depends on pricing-engine quotes, so shorter TTL increases latency.
order-service error rate jumps at the 11:00 bucket.

assumptions: Shorter cache TTL materially increases quote latency enough to cause 5s timeouts
The pricing-engine path is on the failing call chain (errors reference only exchange-gateway)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Predates onset by ~88 min with a 1s TTL delta (F2/F6); no error, metric or timeout references pricing-engine (F8/F9); the failing hop is exchange-gateway's 5000ms upstream connect timeout to the exchange partner, which cfg-2290 cannot touch (F9/F29/F17).

facts.statement: All 349 order-service ERROR logs in 09:00-12:59 were a single signature blaming a downstream: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)', first at 11:02:45Z and last at 12:58:54Z.

exchange-gateway is the origin: its ERROR logs begin 11:01:25Z with 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder', plus 'exchange-api returned 503' from 11:02:20Z and a circuit breaker OPEN warning at 11:03:26Z — ~1 minute before order-service's first 504.
order-service error rate jumped from ~0.2% baseline to ~24.6-31.9% in the 11:00 bucket and held ~30-31%; p99 latency jumped from ~150ms to 4286ms avg (max 5631ms).
exchange-gateway error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 39.33% (11:00 bucket) then ~44.7% steady, and p99 latency from ~130ms to 4625ms avg — matching the 5000ms upstream connect timeout.

exchange-gateway's upstream_latency_ms to the external partner exploded from ~120ms baseline to 7450.9 avg (max 9620.91) at 11:00 and stayed ~9000-9500ms, while its own cpu_pct (~27-32%), memory_pct (~39-49%), request_rate (~245-296 req/s) and restarts (0) stayed flat across onset.

exchange-gateway exposes no connection/db-pool metric ('db-pool_in_use' returned not_found); available metrics are cpu_pct, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts, upstream_error_rate, upstream_latency_ms.

market-data-service, a second and structurally independent caller of exchange-gateway (http edge, no shared datastore with it), degraded in the same 11:01 bucket (~0.24% baseline -> 11:01 avg 3.35 / max 6.44 -> ~6.5% steady) with its only log signature blaming the exchange feed via exchange-gateway (142 WARN 'stale quotes ... via exchange-gateway'), first_seen 11:02:59Z, last 12:57:49Z, and zero ERROR logs; its p99 (~40ms) and request_rate/cpu stayed flat.

Caller-independence test: order-service and market-data-service (two separate exchange-gateway callers, no shared datastore with exchange-gateway) both degraded at 11:01-11:02Z while payment-service (not an exchange-gateway caller) stayed ~0.2% in the same buckets.

H5 (shared ledger-db degradation) is contradicted by measurement: the other ledger-db callers portfolio-service and settlement-service stayed flat at ~0.21% error and flat p99 (no rise at 11:02/11:08/11:14), and ledger-db's only exposed metric cpu_pct is flat (~30%).

No deployment or config change occurred for ANY service in the 10:50-12:59Z onset window (0 deployments, 0 config changes), and exchange-gateway itself had zero deployments and zero config changes in 2026-03-10..03-17T12:59Z.

Exactly one deployment occurred across all services in 06:00-12:59Z: order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333), deployed 10:48:00Z, status 'rolled_back' with rolled_back_at 11:16:00Z; the only config change in the window was pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 (cfg-2290) at 09:20:00Z, ~88 min before onset and with no error/metric/timeout path to the failing hop.

Dependency graph: order-service calls ledger-db, pricing-engine, exchange-gateway and kafka; ledger-db is shared by four services (order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service); redis-cache has no edge to order-service and is therefore not on its submit path; exchange-api is external with has_telemetry:false.

Historical precedent HIST-103 (2025-10-21) matches this signature: 'Order failures during exchange partner outage' across order-service/exchange-gateway with 504 on order submit and upstream timeouts, root cause 'External exchange API outage on the partner side', resolved by failing over to a secondary exchange route.
'inventory-service' does not exist as a monitored component in the system.

assumptions: The 5000ms connect timeout to api.exchange-partner.example reflects partner-side unresponsiveness rather than a network path fault between exchange-gateway and the partner; exchange-api has has_telemetry:false, so the true first failing hop is permanently unobservable from internal data.
The 'exchange-api returned 503' lines originate from the partner side rather than from an intermediary not represented in the dependency graph.
11:00-11:01Z is the true onset rather than a transient cycle; the earliest evidence anywhere is 11:01:25Z and order-service's bucket boundary is 11:00.
The absence of recorded deployments/config changes in the 10:50-12:59Z window implies no unrecorded in-band change to exchange-gateway or the shared components occurred.
market-data-service's 6.5% error_rate is attributable to exchange-gateway calls, inferred from its single WARN signature rather than measured per-call.
The truncation of log queries (40 of 349 order-service, 40 of 473 exchange-gateway, 40 of 142 market-data-service) did not hide an earlier or materially different signature than the ones observed.
kafka and redis-cache, though unmeasured, are not on order-service's failing call path (the failing submit call is HTTP to exchange-gateway, and order-service has no redis-cache edge).

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) Rollback of dep-5333 did NOT coincide with recovery: order-service errors continued to 12:58:54Z (>100 min after the 11:16Z rollback) and exchange-gateway's circuit breaker was OPEN at 11:03:26Z with error rate ~44.7% steady.

timeline.event: Only config change in window: pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 (cfg-2290, config-bot) — ~88 min before onset, no error/metric path to the failing hop.
Only deployment in window: order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333, a.khan, 'Add idempotency keys to order submit') deployed.

order-service error rate jumps from ~0.2% to 24.64% avg (max 31.9) and p99 from ~150ms to 4286ms; exchange-gateway error rate jumps to 39.33% and p99 to 4625ms; exchange-gateway upstream_latency_ms to the partner explodes to 7450.9 avg (max 9620.91).
exchange-gateway first ERROR: 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder' — the earliest evidence of the fault anywhere, at the origin hop.
market-data-service (independent second exchange-gateway caller) error rate jumps in the 11:01 bucket (avg 3.35 / max 6.44), reaching ~6.5% steady, with flat p99 (~40ms).
order-service first 504 log: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' — ~1.5 min after market-data-service onset and ~1 min after the gateway's own first error.
market-data-service first WARN of its only signature: 'stale quotes: exchange feed lag <n>s via exchange-gateway'.
exchange-gateway WARN: 'circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s)'; error rate settles ~44.7% steady.
Incident reported (SEV-1, ~30% order submit failure); on-call begins rollback of v2.15.2.
Rollback does NOT coincide with recovery: order-service errors and the exchange-gateway circuit-breaker-open state persist far beyond this point.
market-data-service last 'stale quotes ... via exchange-gateway' WARN in window (last_match; query truncated at 40 returned).
order-service last 504 log in window — symptom persisting ~100 min after the rollback and ~117 min after onset.

recommended_actions.action: Stop treating order-service rollback as remediation: dep-5333 is already rolled_back (11:16Z) and recovery did not follow. Keep v2.15.2 rolled back only if desired for hygiene, but mark the incident as an external-dependency failure and hand the fix to the exchange-gateway/exchange-partner route.
recommended_actions.rationale: The sole deployment (dep-5333) cannot produce failures in two other never-deployed services (F15/F16/F30/F35); all order-service errors are the single downstream 504 signature (F8) originating at exchange-gateway one minute earlier (F9); errors persisted >100 min after the 11:16Z rollback (F13).

recommended_actions.action: Fail over exchange-gateway to the secondary exchange route (the same resolution recorded for the matching precedent HIST-103), or otherwise divert placeOrder traffic off api.exchange-partner.example; verify by watching exchange-gateway upstream_latency_ms (currently ~9000ms vs ~120ms baseline) and its circuit-breaker state.
recommended_actions.rationale: The stall is on the gateway's upstream call to api.exchange-partner.example (5000ms connect timeouts, 503s from exchange-api, circuit breaker OPEN at 11:03:26Z) while gateway-internal CPU/memory/request_rate/restarts are flat — HIST-103 was resolved exactly by secondary-route failover.

recommended_actions.action: Open a partner-side ticket / escalate to the exchange provider's status channel for api.exchange-partner.example covering ~11:01Z onward, requesting their incident timeline for the placeOrder endpoint and their post-incident report.
recommended_actions.rationale: exchange-api has has_telemetry:false and no change records exist on our side; the partner origin is inferred from exchange-gateway's upstream_latency_ms proxy, so only the vendor can confirm the failing hop.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm recovery end-to-end after failover: exchange-gateway error_rate back toward baseline and circuit breaker CLOSED, then order-service error_rate back to ~0.2% and p99 back to ~150ms, then order-service 504 log rate to zero — do not close the incident on exchange-gateway recovery alone.
recommended_actions.rationale: The observed chain is exchange-gateway upstream stall 11:01:25Z -> market-data-service 11:01 bucket -> order-service first 504 11:02:45Z, and order-service errors were still occurring at 12:58:54Z; recovery must be verified at the reporting service, not just at the origin.

recommended_actions.action: Fix the circuit-breaker / timeout configuration on exchange-gateway so a stuck upstream fails fast: the 5000ms upstream connect timeout plus a 60s-window breaker at failure ratio 0.47 left order-service requests hanging to a ~4.3s p99. Tune the connect timeout and/or lower the breaker trip point so the gateway sheds load to the secondary route automatically.
recommended_actions.rationale: The latency signature is dominated by the stuck upstream call (5000ms connect timeout; gateway p99 4625ms; order-service p99 4286ms) and the breaker only opened at 11:03:26Z, ~2 min after the first timeout and 1 min after order-service's first 504.

recommended_actions.action: Add telemetry (error_rate, latency, availability) for exchange-api / the partner edge, and monitoring on exchange-gateway's upstream_latency_ms plus circuit-breaker state as a first-class alert; the current blind spot is permanent under has_telemetry:false.
recommended_actions.rationale: The true first failing hop is unobservable (exchange-api has_telemetry:false) and every conclusion about the partner rests on exchange-gateway's upstream_latency_ms proxy; a probe/SLO on the partner endpoint would make onset detection immediate rather than inferred.

recommended_actions.action: Automate exchange-route failover and rehearse it: run a game-day for the 'external exchange partner outage' scenario so the secondary route is exercised, and codify a runbook step that distinguishes partner outages from release regressions before initiating rollbacks.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-103 shows this is a recurring failure mode with an existing manual resolution ('failed over to secondary exchange route'); in this incident the first response was a rollback of a deployment that was not the cause and did not restore service (F13/F18).

recommended_actions.action: Improve change/deployment observability so a rollback that does not restore service triggers a dependency-path check automatically (e.g. link deploy events to per-service error-rate and downstream-error signatures). Per-pod rollout timelines and post-rollback error series were unavailable for dep-5333.
recommended_actions.rationale: The 6-minute rollback (10:48Z deploy -> 11:16Z rollback) traded time for no effect because the failure origin was one hop downstream of order-service; capturing rollout timelines and post-change error series would have redirected the response faster.

recommended_actions.action: Close the residual platform-component gap cheaply: query kafka and redis-cache error_rate/latency_p99/cpu_pct for 10:50-12:59Z (and ledger-db's remaining metrics) to convert H5's rank from 'inferred/off-path' to 'contradicted by telemetry'.
recommended_actions.rationale: H5 was demoted largely by structure and by the flatness of the other ledger-db callers (portfolio-service and settlement-service at ~0.21% error with flat p99) plus ledger-db cpu_pct flat ~30%, but kafka and redis-cache were never measured; these queries would remove the last untested alternative.

data_gaps: No telemetry exists for exchange-api (has_telemetry:false, external, owner vendor) or for the partner host api.exchange-partner.example, so the true first failing hop cannot be observed from internal data — the partner-side origin is inferred only from exchange-gateway's upstream_latency_ms proxy.

kafka and redis-cache health metrics (error_rate, latency_p99_ms, cpu_pct, request_rate) for 10:50-12:59Z were never retrieved (tool-call budget exhausted before the kafka query), so H5's kafka and redis-cache legs remain unmeasured; kafka consumer_lag was also not queried.

ledger-db exposes only [connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min]; error_rate, latency_p99_ms and request_rate all returned not_found, so the shared-ledger-db leg is contradicted chiefly by its callers' telemetry rather than by its own latency/error series (replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min and connections_active were not retrieved).

exchange-gateway has no connection/db-pool metric at all, so internal connection-pool exhaustion cannot be disproven directly by a series — only by the absence of any such series, the flat CPU/memory/request_rate/restarts, and the absence of a db edge in the dependency graph.

Log queries were truncated (order-service 40 of 349, exchange-gateway 40 of 473, market-data-service 40 of 142), and no logs were retrieved for api-gateway, exchange-api, bank-partner-api or any datastore, so an earlier cause before 11:01:25Z cannot be ruled out from logs.

No per-pod rollout timeline, canary detail or post-rollback error-rate observations exist for dep-5333, so the exact set of pods that took v2.15.2 and the error trend immediately after 11:16Z are unverified; the persisted-error claim rests on the last error log at 12:58:54Z rather than on a metric series.

No post-12:59Z data exists (current time == latest data) and no metric covers exchange-gateway's recovery after the rollback, so whether the error rate trended to zero or stayed elevated at the time of writing is unknown.

market-data-service exposes no exchange-gateway-specific call metric, so the fraction of its ~6.5% error_rate attributable to exchange-gateway is inferred from its single WARN signature rather than measured per-call.
No baseline comparison for kafka/redis-cache/ledger-db pre-11:00Z buckets was obtainable, so a shared-component deviation at onset versus a normal baseline cannot be shown.
Unverified/low-confidence items in the shared state (F1, F5, F18 as a lead rather than evidence) mean the deployment summary and the HIST-103 precedent are leads and corroboration, not proof.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Evidence that exchange-gateway's upstream_latency_ms to api.exchange-partner.example was only mildly elevated (e.g. ~100-200ms) while its internal CPU/memory/queueing saturated at onset would move the root cause back inside exchange-gateway (a capacity or pool fault) and away from the external partner.

A recorded deployment or config change on exchange-gateway (or on exchange-api) at ~11:00Z — contradicting F14/F17/F19/F23 — would flip this from an external partner outage to a bad change on the gateway itself.

Telemetry showing kafka or redis-cache error_rate/latency/cpu spiking at the 11:00-11:01Z onset would reopen H5, since neither was ever measured; redis-cache would additionally need a path to order-service (currently no edge, F21).

A connection-pool/queue-depth series for exchange-gateway showing exhaustion or backlog at onset would indicate an internal resource fault rather than an unresponsive upstream, invalidating the 'stall is outside the gateway process' inference.

Evidence that exchange-api's 503 responses were generated by an internal intermediary (e.g. a gateway-side proxy or rate limiter) rather than the partner side would relocate the failing hop from the partner into our own estate.

Verified telemetry for market-data-service showing its errors are NOT exchange-gateway-related (e.g. an independent internal cause) would break the caller-independence argument (F30-F35), the strongest evidence that the fault is at exchange-gateway/exchange-api rather than on the order-service path.
A metric series showing order-service error_rate recovering to baseline immediately at/after the 11:16Z rollback would contradict F13 and restore H1/H3 (release-related) as a viable explanation.

A network-path fault between exchange-gateway and the partner (packet loss, DNS/TLS failure on our egress) would substitute a network cause for partner-side unresponsiveness, though it would not change the recommended failover mitigation.
